note: How a week becomes a meeting — the branch meeting builder, for rickyrampersadbranch.com/meetings. Written 14 October 2026, after the first cut was taken off the site: its bed came from a track whose licence was never established, it carried a blue substitute mark instead of the branch's gold shield, it ran the week Monday to Sunday, and it said the figures came from Salesforce. The branch manager set the shape: the week runs Sunday to Sunday, the figures are read from the Branch Portfolio, an agent checks their own data once a day, and Wednesday is where that data gets argued. The page is meetings/builder-film.html, built by hand; this file is its script, voice-lines.py voices and times it, and builder-timing.py writes the durations back onto the page. Nothing here is a real client, a real agent or a real figure.

scenes.line: The branch meets on a Wednesday morning. Ninety minutes. The meeting is built before anybody walks in.
It is built out of the week you already worked.
The week runs Sunday to Sunday. On Sunday evening it closes. The figures freeze, and nothing moves under a number that has already been read out.

scenes.scene: Sunday 20:00 — the Branch Portfolio is read
scenes.line: Then the Branch Portfolio is read. Applications in. Policies issued. What is still sitting, and what is owed.
Sales support adds the rest. Every renewal, every claim and every questionnaire is a line in the record.

scenes.scene: every working morning — your own data
scenes.line: Every working morning you get your own data. What is still on your list. Where you stand against your target. Nobody else's figures, and nobody else sees yours.
At ten, the first check goes out.

scenes.scene: fifteen seconds — tap what you did
scenes.line: Fifteen seconds. Tap what you did. Prospecting. Calls. A client seen. A fact find. Nothing to type unless you want to.
At three, the afternoon. While you still remember it.
Nobody writes a report. The week writes itself.

scenes.scene: Wednesday 07:00 — the builder reads it all
scenes.line: At seven on Wednesday the builder reads all of it. It knows who worked, and on what.
It knows which numbers moved, and which did not.

scenes.scene: and who has not presented lately
scenes.line: It knows who has not presented lately. So it asks them.
And it writes the agenda. Eleven items. Ninety minutes. A name against every one.
Nine o'clock. Everybody logs in. The login is the register.
You open the meeting. Your own item is already at the top.
Three minutes past, the branch manager takes last week's open items, by name and by date. Nothing new is raised until those are spoken to.
Ten past, sales support. Applications in, applications issued, and what is still sitting, with the oldest one named.
Twenty past, the B M E takes the unit round. Everybody with something moving says what moved.
Ten to ten, one case in somebody's own words. Chosen by the rota, not by the chair.
A guest opens their own link and joins the same agenda. They see this meeting, and nothing else of the branch.
And every single week, every person in the room names one client. About twenty seconds each. Nobody leaves without naming one.
On Thursday the actions are chased. And the week starts again.
The week builds the meeting.
Wednesday, nine to half past ten. Ricky Rampersad Branch dot com, slash meetings.
